Explanation

How it works

The rules are written once, summarised for the AI pilot, and checked on every command before it reaches the autopilot.

The architecture

The system the grant specifies. Each box links to the work package that builds it.

  1. Operator / mission — Gives the task prompt: what the drone should do.
  2. VLA backend — AI model: camera image and words in, 4-D action out at 10 Hz.
  3. Policy IR / bundle — The rules, parsed and sealed with a hash, loaded by the Shield.
  4. Prefix Compiler — Turns the rules into a short pack (CSP) placed in front of the VLA prompt.
  5. Safety Shield (ROS 2 node) — Last software layer: checks, repairs or stops each action before MAVROS 2.
  6. MAVROS 2 — ROS 2 bridge that turns Shield output into MAVLink messages for ArduPilot.
  7. ArduPilot (SITL / firmware) — The autopilot: runs the inner control loop at 100-400 Hz.
  8. GeoFence / RTL / Land backstop — ArduPilot's own fence: the final safety net if the Shield fails.
  9. Stress Testing harness — Runs many scenarios, changes rules mid-flight and computes the KPIs for the final report.
  10. Ground station (Mission Planner) — Operator's map view of the flight, fed through mavlink-router next to MAVROS 2.

One Shield tick

Ten times a second, every command goes through the same six steps.

  1. Predict
    Assume the command is kept, and forecast at constant velocity where the drone will be over the next seconds.
  2. Check
    Check the command against every active rule: speed, climb and turn rate; altitude band; no-fly zones; corridor; obstacle clearance from a distance map; stand-off from the tracked target. An invalid value (NaN or infinity) counts as a violation. A clean command passes unchanged.
  3. Repair
    Fix the command with small operators: the speed, climb and yaw clamps first, then the altitude fix, then up to 3 passes of clearance fix, stand-off recovery, corridor return and geofence slide. It stops as soon as the result checks clean; the passes repeat because one fix can break another.
  4. Re-check
    Check the repaired command again. If it still breaks a P0 rule, look for a recovery heading that checks clean. The last check is always on the command actually sent.
  5. Brake
    If no repair checks clean and stopping is legal, send Brake: every velocity value (vx, vy, vz and yaw rate) set to zero. If stopping would itself break a rule, send the best recovery heading.
  6. Log
    Every tick on which the Shield found or fixed something is written to the audit log with the policy hash, the raw and sent commands, and any violation left in the sent command.

The city demonstration

In the Project AirSim city a drone follows a red car. This is the chain from the camera to the motors. A hand-written controller is the pilot here, so this demonstration exercises perception, the Shield and the policy indicator.

  1. Drone camera

    Front camera: colour and depth images, 10 per second.

  2. Detector (OWL-ViT)

    Finds boxes that match a phrase such as 'a red car'.

  3. Identity check

    Uses depth and the map to judge whether a box can physically be the car.

  4. Tracker

    Locks one car, estimates where it is, and takes it back only on evidence.

  5. Pilot (hand-written)

    Hand-written controller, not a VLA: follows the car's trail about 20 m behind.

  6. FenceGuard

    Lets the pilot read the policy, so it slows or steers around zones by itself.

  7. Safety Shield

    Checks every command against all rules, then passes, repairs or brakes it.

  8. Simulator autopilot

    Project AirSim's own flight controller flies the command; ArduPilot is not used here.

  9. Policy HUD

    On-screen panel: each rule, its limit, the live value and a status colour.

Reading the policy indicator

A frame from the flight of 3 Oct 2026. Select a number to read what that part of the screen shows.

123456
  1. Flight status — Time, altitude, bearing to the target, forward speed, distance to the target, and the tracking state. Green 'TARGET LOCKED' means the tracker holds the car. Here: t 39.0 s, altitude 10.1 m, separation 21.2 m.
  2. Event banner — The most important event of the last 1.5 s. Here it reads 'NO-FLY ZONE AHEAD - ROUTING AROUND IT (nfz-frontage)' in blue: the pilot (FenceGuard) is steering around the zone by itself, so the Shield does not need to act.
  3. Rule panel — One row per rule in the loaded policy (follow-car-citylife-nfz v0.1.0): name, limit, value measured now, status. Example row: Altitude band, 6-14 m, now 10.1 m, OK.
  4. Rule status — Status word and dot colour per rule. Here the NFZ row is AVOID (4 m away), the 10 m pedestrian rule is idle because the target is a car, and obstacle clearance is NEAR (4.5 m against a 3 m limit).
  5. Running counts — Totals so far in this flight: Shield corrections, brakes, holds and P0 escapes (ticks on which a P0 violation remained in the command sent).
  6. Map — North-up map, 80 m across: obstacles (dark), the red NFZ, the drone's track (blue line, white arrow) and a red dot, which is the tracker's estimate of the car, not ground truth.

Rule status colours

  • idle — The rule is in the policy but cannot apply now, e.g. the 10 m pedestrian stand-off while the target is a car.
  • OK — The rule applies and is met with room to spare.
  • NEAR — Inside the rule's own soft margin, within the pilot's 12 m brake distance of an NFZ, or off the obstacle map (clearance unknown).
  • AVOID — The pilot (FenceGuard) is steering around an NFZ or obstacle by itself; the Shield does not need to act.
  • HOLD — The pilot stopped short of an NFZ or obstacle.
  • ACTING — The Shield repaired the command for this rule.
  • BREACH — The drone is past the limit now (inside the zone or its margin, too close, or outside the band), or a P0 rule is still violated by the command actually sent.
  • BRAKE — Repair did not converge and the Shield stopped the drone.

Where the software runs

The grant names three topologies. The same Shield code is meant to move from one to the next.

dev

Everything on one desktop

ArduPilot SITL, the simulators, MAVROS 2, the Shield and the pilot run together. Used for development and tests; the Shield on/off runs on this site come from here.

In use

hil

Simulators on the desktop, VLA and Shield on a Jetson Orin

The desktop runs the simulators, ArduPilot SITL, MAVROS 2 and the ground station; the Orin runs the VLA and the Shield over the network. The grant measures its KPIs in this topology.

Next

flight

On the drone

The Orin runs the VLA and the Shield as a companion computer next to the real ArduPilot autopilot. Planned to run the same software as hil.
